notes: Background: Tidecraft builds in-product personalization and analytics for mid-market e-commerce platforms. Heavy usage during drop events and release windows.
Sales motion: started on Hosted API trial (free credits) to validate latency and quality; positive engagement from PM and infra leads.
POC metrics (hosted trial, 14 days): ~450k tokens consumed, avg QPS 3.6, observed peak QPS 12 (sustained ~3m), 95p concurrency ~28 during a simulated 'drop' test.
Token mix observed in trial: ~60% short chat (~<=150 tokens total), ~30% medium (~151-800 tokens), ~10% long (>800 tokens) — embeddings accounted for ~15% of calls by count but ~5% of tokens.
Latency SLOs requested: p95 < 150ms for short chat (50-150 tokens), p95 < 1200ms for long calls. Customer cares about consistent p95 more than occasional p99 spikes.
Model preferences: open-models preferred to avoid vendor lock (we discussed quantized Llama-family 33B/70B, Mistral-like candidates). Quality validation via Redwood eval harness is important to them.
Security: Must integrate with Okta SSO (SAML), require audit logging retention 1 year, KMS-backed key control for any Dedicated deployment, and EU data residency for EU customers.
Quote from CTO: 'If we can hit 120ms p95 for our short flows and keep unit cost within our forecast, Dedicated makes sense — but we need clear sizing numbers and a predictable burst model.'
Cost sensitivity: mid-market — willing to commit to monthly Dedicated if unit economics show >30% cost reduction vs hosted at projected volumes.
Redwood-specific asks: show predicted token/sec per GPU for proposed model variant, recommended autoscale headroom, and a simple fallback plan to smaller models for peak events.
Internal stakeholders: PM (Eva Chen) -> product feature owner; Infra lead (Marcus Liu) -> responsible for VPC setup and peering; Finance (Liam O'Neal) -> procurement touchpoint.
Open legal items: finalize DPA clauses around data residency and subprocessor list; procurement expects a standard 60-day SLA review cycle.
Preference: start Dedicated with a single pool that can autoscale + a burst buffer to Hosted during heavy events; want canary rollout for model updates.
Actionable: AE + SE to provide Dedicated sizing deck with both steady-state and 3x-peak headroom, include cost comparison sheet (hosted vs dedicated) and a three-month rollout timeline.
Notes style: shorthand used in internal logs — see timeline for meeting links / IDs.

sizing_forecast_summary: Customer asks for Dedicated sizing that meets steady-state 8 QPS with 3x burst to 25 QPS. Based on trial token mix (60% short ~120 tokens, 30% medium ~450 tokens, 10% long ~1800 tokens) and expected growth (x3 in 12 months), recommended starting pool: 2 x A100-equivalent GPU nodes (80GB) with autoscale policy + burst capacity backed by hosted. Expected baseline throughput ~120k tokens/min with headroom for 3x peaks; estimated monthly commit to hit target ARR range. SE to deliver GPU-level tokens/sec benchmarks by model variant.
